Target Business Services
Location: 9 Limbee Gld, Huntingdale, WA 6110
Salary: $80,000 Plus 12% Superannuation
Position: Full Time, Permanent

Our client, Khosa Concrete & Landscaping Pty Ltd, located in Huntingdale, Western Australia, is a growing construction business specialising in high-quality concreting, landscaping and outdoor construction solutions throughout the Perth metropolitan area. The company delivers a broad range of residential and commercial projects, including concrete driveways, pathways, patios, retaining walls, paving, fencing, timber structures, artificial turf installations and complete landscape transformations. 

Due to continued business growth and an increasing volume of construction projects, our client is seeking an experienced and motivated Carpenter to join its skilled construction team. The successful applicant will undertake a variety of carpentry works associated with building interiors, outdoor living spaces and structural construction, while ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications to determine materials, dimensions and installation requirements. 
-	Measure, cut, shape, assemble and install timber, plywood and other building materials to required specifications. 
-	Construct, install and repair timber frameworks, wall frames, floor systems, roof structures, partitions and ceilings. 
-	Install doors, windows, skirting boards, architraves, staircases, cabinetry and other interior and exterior timber fittings. 
-	Build and install pergolas, decking, fencing, gates and other outdoor timber structures. 
-	Carry out first-fix and second-fix carpentry works for residential and commercial building projects. 
-	Undertake formwork construction where required to support building and landscaping projects. 
-	Repair and maintain existing timber structures, fixtures and fittings to ensure structural integrity and appearance. 
-	Operate, maintain and inspect carpentry tools, machinery and equipment in a safe and efficient manner. 
-	Estimate material requirements and assist in ordering timber and construction materials. 
-	Ensure all carpentry works comply with Australian building codes, project specifications and workplace health and safety requirements. 
-	Liaise professionally with clients, supervisors and other trades to ensure projects are completed on time and to a high standard.

Skills & Qualifications

-	AQF Certificate III in Carpentry (or equivalent trade qualification), including at least two years of structured on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV in a relevant trade.
-	Minimum one year of relevant full-time experience as a Carpenter.
-	Ability to accurately read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications.
-	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building materials and safe work practices.
-	High attention to detail with excellent workmanship and problem-solving abilities.
-	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
-	Good organisational and time management skills with the ability to meet project deadlines.
-	Sound understanding of Australian Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.
To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au

Location: Darwin NT
Employment Type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Salary: AUD $67,510 – $75,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on skills and experience

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
The business (ABN 53 603 812 004) is a Darwin-based professional cleaning business servicing commercial, industrial and government clients across the Northern Territory. We provide duct cleaning, air-conditioning cleaning and maintenance, kitchen exhaust cleaning, cool room cleaning, mould remediation, inspection reporting and cleaning schedules.
We are looking for a General Clerk to support our office, administration and customer service functions.

About the Role
The General Clerk will perform general clerical and administrative duties to support daily business operations. The role will assist with customer enquiries, job records, technician paperwork, service reports, filing, data entry and general office support.

The successful applicant will:
- Record, prepare, sort, classify and file customer, supplier and job information.
- Maintain digital and paper records for cleaning, HVAC, duct, mould and maintenance jobs.
- Answer telephone calls, emails and customer enquiries.
- Provide customers with basic information about services, bookings and job documentation.
- Prepare routine documents, job records, service reports and internal summaries.
- Enter customer details, job information and technician notes into business systems.
- Proofread and correct routine emails, forms, reports and service documents.
- Assist with scheduling records, site access paperwork and technician job paperwork.
- Scan, copy, upload and file documents, photos and completion evidence.
- Sort incoming and outgoing mail and office documents.
- Assist with reception duties and general office administration.
- Maintain confidentiality of customer, staff and business records.

Applicants should have:
- Experience in clerical, office administration, reception, customer service or data entry work.
- Good computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office or similar systems.
- Good attention to detail and accurate data entry skills.
- Ability to organise records and manage routine paperwork.
- Clear communication skills.
- Ability to work with customers, technicians, suppliers and management.
- Ability to manage several administrative tasks at the same time.

Applicants should have:
- Certificate II or III in Business, Business Administration or a related field; or
- At least 1 year of relevant clerical or administrative experience.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable and organised administration professional who can support our office operations, maintain accurate records, assist with customer enquiries, and help keep our cleaning and maintenance jobs running smoothly.

To apply, submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.
If you are interested in joining a practical, professional team that delivers specialist HVAC, duct, exhaust, mould and commercial cleaning services across the Northern Territory, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 1 August 2026

Immediate start | Temp initial 6 months | hybrid working   Your new company     Our client is a rapidly growing, purpose-led organisation committed to supporting vulnerable communities across Australia. Following a period of significant transformation, the business is continuing its growth journey through service expansion, workforce growth, systems enhancement and operational improvement. With ambitious plans for the future, the organisation is investing in its people, capability and technical infrastructure to support sustainable growth. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Senior People & Culture Business Partner to join at a pivotal stage and play a key role in shaping and strengthening the people function.    Your new role     As Senior People & Culture Business Partner, you will join the business during a period of growth, change and continuous improvement. Partnering closely with leaders across the organisation, you will help drive key people initiatives, support operational excellence and contribute to the development of scalable people practices and frameworks. This is a business that's very much in a phase of "creating the plane while flying it." As such, we're looking for someone who thrives in evolving environments, can comfortably navigate ambiguity, and enjoys bringing structure, process and practical solutions while maintaining momentum.   Leadership will be an important aspect of the role, particularly during periods of transition, but this is ultimately a hands-on position requiring someone who is equally comfortable leading initiatives as they are rolling up their sleeves and delivering outcomes.    Key responsibilities include:  
 
 Partnering with leaders across the business to provide expert People & Culture advice and support. 
 Supporting the development and implementation of HR systems, processes and frameworks that enable organisational growth. 
 Leading and delivering key people projects and change initiatives. 
 Managing employee relations, investigations, performance management and industrial relations matters. 
 Contributing to upcoming workforce changes, including award updates, remuneration reviews and compliance requirements. 
 Reviewing and updating position descriptions, policies and people processes. 
 Ensuring compliance with Fair Work legislation, workplace policies and relevant awards. 
 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Significant experience in senior HR, People & Culture Business Partner or HR leadership roles.   
 Strong Employee Relations and Industrial Relations expertise, with the confidence to manage complex and sensitive people matters.   
 Proven experience delivering people initiatives, systems improvements and change projects within community service environments   
 Strong leadership capability, with the confidence to provide guidance, support and direction during periods of growth and transition.   
 A hands-on, pragmatic and solutions-focused approach, with a willingness to roll up your sleeves and get things done.    
 Experience with SCHADS Award is highly desirable.    
 Experience with EmploymentHero and Asana is a plus.     
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Immediate start opportunity.   
 Initial 6-month contract   
 Attractive day-rate   
 Hybrid working arrangements based in Melbourne.    
 
 The opportunity to join a purpose-driven organisation making a meaningful impact in the community.

SEO Manager (AKA Digital Experience Manager, Associate Digital Experience Director)
As Search Engine Optimisation Manager, you’ll be focused on delivering best in class SEO driving business growth across a portfolio of clients. This requires strong experience in SEO strategy and implementation. A good understanding of Paid Search is also required to implement holistic search strategies. 

We’re looking for a talented Manager who is also a delight to work with, which usually includes: 

•	A degree in marketing, advertising, business or a related field 
•	+4 years of combined experience in organic and paid search, digital project management or account management 
•	Proven experience managing a team
•	Experience scoping projects, providing forecasts and driving ongoing process improvement
•	The ability to create and implement SEO strategies frameworks that successfully deliver incremental growth overtime. 
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills – and a knack for details
•	Experience developing content strategies and competitor analysis using a range of platform and technologies. 
•	Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously and make smart, fast decisions 
•	Knowledge of HTML, JavaScript, and CSS, with a focus on optimizing them for SEO
•	Stellar communication and presentation skills – you’re poised, articulate and convincing
•	Previous experience with SEO industry tools – i.e. Google Analytics, Omniture, Google Search Console, Brightedge, SEMRush, Ahrefs and Screaming Frog.
Salary: $90K - $120K package

SEO Director (Digital Experience Director, Director of SEO, SEO Lead, Head of SEO)
As Director of SEO, you’ll grow the division and develop a strategic vision, whilst providing leadership to the team.  You’ll build the agency’s search practice (SEO) to support aggressive revenue growth.
 
Day to day, your responsibilities will include:
•	Directing long-term and short-term strategic marketing efforts to meet both market share and sales goals for clients via SEO strategies
•	Helping to assess and pursue new business opportunities while maintaining the company’s existing strengths 
•	Developing a world-class search marketing team that will scale and thrive as the business grows
•	Effectively using tools to automate and scale the business in an efficient, cost-effective manner 
•	Ensuring excellence and accuracy in all client deliverables and working with Managers/Directors to present them
•	Developing or approving all scopes of work that include search engine optimization
•	Collaborating with Delivery Managers on project timelines and with Staffing on resource needs
Salary: over threshold 

This role requires; deep familiarity with the digital environment and an understanding of business from both market and P&L perspectives, Strong analytical and problem solving skills, knowledge of HTML, JavaScript, and CSS and outstanding leadership and people management skills. 
All roles require a relevant tertiary qualification or a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in lieu of qualification.

This role enables flexible working arrangements.     Your new role    In this exciting role, you will be:

 Assisting with the delivery of infrastructure projects. 
 Acting as an escalation point for junior members of the IT team. 
 Contributing to cyber awareness training and managing internal phishing campaigns. 
 Maintaining and developing documentation and knowledge base articles. 
 
   What you'll need to succeed    To be successful in your application, you will need: 
 
 Prior experience in providing level 2 end-user IT support in a corporate setting. 
 Sound knowledge of Windows 10 / 11, Active Directory, Windows Server, Office 365, Intune / SCCM, AVD / Citrix, PowerShell scripting and Network troubleshooting. 
 Highly developed troubleshooting and problem-solving skills. 
 A tertiary education in Information Technology, as well as Azure, Microsoft and ITIL certifications are beneficial.

   What you'll get in return    Working in an organisation where they develop and grow careers, you will be offered an excellent salary package, in a role that offers exposure to leading technologies and projects. This organisation prides itself on internal promotion and career development and offers development training. Do not miss out!

result.description:
Position: Retail Manager
Type: Full-time
Employer: IN2 FONES PTY LTD
Location: Mount Vernon NSW 2178
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
IN2 FONES PTY LTD is a dynamic and expanding telecommunications retail business that operates multiple Vodafone-branded stores and customer service operations across New South Wales. With a recent growth to approximately 10 stores, the company specialises in delivering high-quality mobile phones, tablets, smart watches, service plans, accessories, and repair services to a diverse customer base. Known for its strong focus on customer satisfaction, operational excellence, and market competitiveness, IN2 FONES fosters a supportive and performance-driven workplace culture that values teamwork, professional development, and innovation in the fast-paced retail telecom sector.
About the Position:
The Retail Manager plays a pivotal leadership role in overseeing the day-to-day operations of three telecommunications retail stores within IN2 FONES PTY LTD. This position is responsible for driving sales, profitability, and operational efficiency while implementing strategic initiatives to enhance market presence and customer experience. The role is essential for supporting the company’s continued expansion and achieving business objectives in a competitive retail environment.
Key Responsibilities:
Direct and control the day-to-day operations of three telecommunications retail stores to ensure the achievement of sales, profitability and operational objectives.
Determine product mix, pricing strategies and stock levels for mobile phones, tablets, smart watches, telecommunications service plans, accessories and repair services in accordance with market demand and business objectives.
Develop and implement purchasing, sales and marketing strategies, including promotional campaigns and bundled product offers, to increase revenue and strengthen market competitiveness.
Manage procurement, inventory planning, stock control, stock reconciliation and loss prevention across all retail locations to ensure product availability and minimise inventory shrinkage.
Analyse sales reports, financial results and key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify business trends, improve operational efficiency and maximise profitability.
Prepare and manage store budgets, monitor operating expenses and implement cost-control measures to achieve financial performance targets.
Recruit, supervise, train, roster and manage the performance of retail staff across all store locations to ensure operational efficiency and achievement of business objectives.
Oversee visual merchandising, product displays and promotional activities to maximise product visibility, sales performance and brand consistency.
Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety legislation, company policies, retail procedures and all relevant regulatory requirements.
Liaise with senior management to implement business strategies, improve operational processes and support the continued commercial growth of the business.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Diploma level qualification (or equivalent).
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Proven leadership and team management skills with the ability to recruit, train, motivate and develop retail staff.
Strong commercial acumen, including experience in sales target achievement, inventory management, budgeting, and profit optimisation.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with a customer-focused mindset and ability to build positive relationships.
Analytical skills to interpret sales data, KPIs, and financial reports to drive informed decision-making.
Knowledge of retail operations in telecommunications or a similar fast-paced consumer goods environment.
Commitment to compliance, workplace health and safety, and high ethical standards.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
result.title: Retail Manager

result.description:
Regional Restaurant Manager – Bronte NSW

Kogan People Solutions, recruiters, are working to assist our client who runs a highly regarded Brazilian restaurant group based in Bronte, NSW. Renowned for delivering authentic Brazilian cuisine while incorporating premium Australian ingredients, our client has built a strong reputation as one of Sydney's leading Brazilian dining destinations. Due to continued growth and expansion, an exciting opportunity has become available for an experienced Restaurant Manager to oversee the operations of multiple restaurant locations. 

The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring operational excellence, maintaining consistent service standards, and driving the commercial success of multiple venues while supporting the continued growth of the business.

•	Location: Based in Bronte, NSW with travel across other venues as needed.

•	Employment Type: Full-time, ongoing

•	Salary: Negotiable in the range $140k – $145k per annum plus superannuation

Key responsibilities include:

•	Oversee the day-to-day operations of the base venue at Bronte and multiple restaurant locations, ensuring consistent service quality, food standards, and operational efficiency.

•	Lead, mentor, and support local Managers and restaurant teams to achieve business objectives and maintain a positive workplace culture.

•	Recruit, train, develop, and performance-manage management and front-of-house staff across all venues.

•	Develop staffing strategies and coordinate workforce planning, rostering, and labour cost management across multiple sites.

•	Monitor financial performance, including budgets, revenue, labour costs, food and beverage costs, and profitability, implementing strategies to improve results.

•	Analyse sales reports and key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify trends and opportunities for business improvement.

•	Ensure compliance with food safety regulations, liquor licensing requirements, workplace health and safety legislation, and company policies across all locations.

•	Maintain exceptional customer service standards and promptly resolve customer feedback and operational issues.

•	Coordinate with kitchen leadership to ensure menu consistency, quality control, and efficient service delivery.

•	Work closely with senior management to develop and implement business growth strategies, promotional campaigns, and operational improvements.

•	Manage supplier relationships, inventory control, purchasing processes, and stock management across multiple venues.

•	Conduct regular site visits and operational audits to ensure brand consistency, cleanliness, presentation, and compliance with company standards.

•	Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance customer satisfaction, employee engagement, and operational performance.

•	Prepare regular operational and financial reports for senior management, providing recommendations to improve business outcomes.

Skills & Experience Required to be considered:

•	Diploma or higher in Business, Management, Commerce or a closely related discipline or agreed substitute.

•	Have at least 1, or more years (preferably more) professional experience managing multiple hospitality venues simultaneously.

•	Strong leadership, coaching, and people management skills with the ability to build high-performing teams.

•	Excellent financial acumen, including budgeting, cost control, forecasting, and profitability management.

•	Thorough understanding of hospitality operations, food safety requirements, and workplace compliance.

•	Excellent organisational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

•	Ability to work in a fast-paced environment while managing competing priorities across multiple locations.

•	Experience with hospitality POS systems, rostering software, and business reporting tools.

•	Relevant hospitality or business management qualifications are highly regarded.

•	Available across the working week including weekends

•	Proven ability to prioritise, set goals and have the determination to achieve them.

•	You must have unrestricted rights to work full time in Australia to apply for this position.

Applications

Please respond to the recruiters using the facilities on this site, and ensure you attach your updated CV.

Kogan People Solutions are grateful for all applications, but kindly note that they will only respond to shortlisted applicants.

Kogan People Solutions – recruitment excellence
